title: Design of Manchester Carry Chain Hybrid Adder for MASH 1-1-1 Delta Sigma Modulator for Fractional-N Frequency Synthesizers
problem: MASH 1-1-1 Delta Sigma Modulators for fractional-N frequency synthesizers require high-speed, low-power adders with minimal worst-case delay.
motivation: Fractional-N synthesizers are critical for frequency synthesis; MASH DSM quality depends on adder performance (speed, power, jitter).
method: When adding numbers in a circuit, carry propagation—where each bit must wait for the previous bit's result—creates the main delay bottleneck. This design speeds it up by combining two techniques: Carry-Look-Ahead predicts what each carry bit will be without sequential waiting, while Carry-Select pre-computes results assuming both possible carry values and instantly selects the right one. The implementation uses Domino Logic (a fast circuit style that trades increased power for lower delay) and routes carry signals through a Manchester Carry Chain (an optimized pathway design). It includes a low-power partially static flip-flop (a hybrid between fully dynamic and fully static logic) that samples the result on the falling clock edge.
key_novelty: The core innovation is combining Carry-Look-Ahead and Carry-Select in a Manchester Carry Chain topology using Domino Logic.
contributions: Hybrid CLA-Carry-Select adder for MASH DSM
Manchester Carry Chain topology in Domino Logic
Low-power partially static flip-flop for output sampling
Designed and verified in Xilinx Vivado (Zedboard) and TSMC 65nm CMOS
limitations: Abstract only; no comparison with other high-speed adders; silicon area not reported; full MASH DSM performance metrics (SNR, THD) not provided.
